subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write the differences between 'open' and 'closed' systems of circulation.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.48, VSAQ 61. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Text revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the insider note no longer says how a difference without examples is marked, and states what a complete answer contains instead.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Open circulation
steps.why: With no capillaries the blood leaves the vessels and bathes the organs directly, so the pressure stays low.
common_mistakes: Writing that there are no vessels at all. There are vessels and sinuses.
steps.memory_tip: Open means the blood leaves the pipes into open spaces.
steps.margin_note: One line for the definition, one for the examples.
lines: In the open type of circulation, blood

steps.label: Closed circulation
steps.why: Blood kept inside vessels can be pushed at high pressure and sent where it is needed, which is why active animals have it.
common_mistakes: Leaving out capillaries. Their presence is the marking difference.
Naming arthropods here. They have the open type.
steps.memory_tip: Closed means the blood never leaves the pipes.
steps.margin_note: Keep the two types on separate lines so the contrast shows.
lines: In the closed type of circulation, blood

insider_note: Give an example group for each type. The complete answer states the structural difference — sinuses and no capillaries against vessels with capillaries — and names an example group on each side.
